title: Chapter 287: No Matter What You Hear, Don't Come Out
html:
“Sir, I’m an outdoor livestreamer. I explore unusual places for my audience.” Afraid the old man would not believe him, Chen Ge took out his phone and opened a page containing his videos. “I’m fairly well known online. You can search for my name if you’d like.”

The unfamiliar terms only confused the old man. “Search for you? You’re standing right in front of me.”

He tightened his grip on the hoe and regarded Chen Ge with alarm.

“Put simply, I’m a famous explorer,” Chen Ge summarized, no longer caring whether the old man understood. He produced a banknote. “I became lost while exploring these mountains. I’m fortunate to have found you. Could you tell me how to return to Jiujiang?”

The old man made no move toward the money. He kept his wary gaze fixed on Chen Ge. As they faced each other in the orchard, the capricious mountain weather shifted. A chill entered the air, followed by rain.

“Rain?” Chen Ge held out a palm to catch the drops. If the downpour intensified, traveling through the mountains would become far more dangerous.

“I don’t know where you came from, but this is Lin Guan Village, halfway between Jiujiang and Linjiang. We’re far from the city, and no vehicles pass nearby. Returning to Jiujiang won’t be easy.” The old man leaned against his hoe, his legs still weak from the shock of finding a stranger behind him in the middle of the night.

“Then what am I supposed to do?” Chen Ge arranged his features into a convincing mask of worry.

“I can lead you to the foot of the mountain, but the journey will probably take all night.” The old man sighed. “There’s a village below. I can take you that far, but don’t enter it. Go straight to the main road.”

“Why can’t I enter the village? If there are some villagers, I don’t mind spending a night there.”

“Just listen to me! Why do you have so many questions?” the old man said sternly. This seemed to be especially important.

“You said yourself that no cars come here. Even if I reach the foot of the mountain, I still won’t be able to return to Jiujiang. And it looks ready to pour. I’ll need somewhere to shelter, won’t I?” Chen Ge’s argument was reasonable, leaving the old man without a reply. He merely glared as the silence lengthened.

As the rain intensified, the old man sighed. “This weather will bring heavy mist by morning. If you don’t mind the conditions, you can stay with me tonight.”

He took the lamp from the branch and dragged his hoe several meters before looking back. “Are you truly a famous explorer?”

“Why would I lie?” Chen Ge did not feel afraid even though the old man could assault him with the hoe. He took out his phone with one hand while his other reached for the hammer inside his backpack. “You can search for me online. Look, this is me.”

Chen Ge showed the video of himself inside the Third Sick Hall. It was the most normal video of himself that he could find.

“You’ve been on television before?”

“I suppose you can say that. I’m considered quite famous in Jiujiang.”

After comparing Chen Ge with the man in the video and scanning the comments beneath it, the old man nodded. “That explains it. No ordinary person would come here so late.”

Realizing he might have revealed too much, he shouldered the hoe and continued walking. “Follow me.”

They left the peach orchard and, after several minutes, arrived at four wooden huts.

“You can use the first hut. Once the lights go out, stay inside. No matter what you hear, do not come out.” The old man unlocked its door but kept the key.

“That sounds scary. Is it because there are wolves here?” Chen Ge came up with a lie. “I hear wolf attacks are common in the mountains…”

“There are no wolves. Lie down and sleep. Nothing will happen as long as you remain inside.” The old man ushered him into the hut, then repeated, “Remember: don’t come out. Don’t even put your head or hand outside. Understood?”

“Don’t worry. I scare easily. I would never deliberately put myself in danger.” Chen Ge sat obediently on the wooden bed.

“Good. Then rest well. When the morning mist disappears tomorrow morning, I’ll lead you out of the mountain.” After the old man bade Chen Ge farewell, he entered the second wooden hut.

This place is deeply strange.Chen Ge surveyed the room. Its only piece of furniture was a bare wooden bed without so much as a blanket. The hut had clearly stood vacant for years. Dust covered every surface, and spiderwebs choked the corners.

How could anyone live here? Did he deliberately place me in this hut, or is something wrong with all four?Chen Ge inspected the door and noticed an unsettling detail. Rather than being fitted on the inside, its lock was mounted outside.

He told me not to leave, but the door can’t even be locked from the inside.Chen Ge felt like the old man had to be hiding something from him. He leaned against the door and yelled at the hut opposite, “Sir! I still don’t know your name!”

“Keep your voice down! I’m not deaf.” The old man’s voice trembled, as though he feared attracting something. “My surname is Bai. Now go to sleep!”

“Okay.”

After twenty minutes, Chen Ge yelled at the hut next door again, “Master Bai, are you there?”

“What now?!”

“Nothing, I just want to thank you and wish you a healthy life!”

“Go to sleep!”

Chen Ge leaned against the wall, his expression grave. Every twenty minutes, he called to the neighboring hut. Someone repeatedly awakened would normally sound angry or groggy, yet Master Bai’s replies contained neither emotion. He had never fallen asleep, and his voice trembled each time. It seemed less as though he was resting than waiting for something to arrive.

Master Bai appears honest, and he even warned me about the village below. He doesn’t seem malicious, but his strange behavior is troubling.Chen Ge silently eased the door open a crack. Rain poured through the darkness outside.

These four huts should be Jiang Ling’s family’s old home, but it’s unclear which one is the hut where her parents died.

He started the recorder and closed one hand around the hammer inside his backpack. Instead of remaining in his hut, he crept toward the other three.

The rain swallowed his footsteps. Hammer in hand, Chen Ge stopped outside Master Bai’s hut and pressed an ear to the door.
